alignments.note: The verbless clause's possessive לְ carries the *hath* (rule 43).
The article assimilated into the pointed preposition takes the written *the* (rules 12, 15).

Comparative מִן rendered by the two-word English comparative *more than*; headed on *than*, the word carrying the comparative relation, while *more* is the degree word English writes beside it (rule 24). This corrects the verse pass's head on *more*, which read rule 24's `מִן` → *out of* → *out* as a preference for the opening word: there the opening word carries the ablative lexeme and *of* is the bare connective, and here it is the other way about. ECC.6.5's *rather than* is headed on *than* in this same chapter, and the corpus aligns מִן to *more than* headed on *than* in twenty-five units and to a bare *than* in a hundred and nineteen. Heading on *more* was the competing reading and is not taken.
The ASV supplies a coordinator between two juxtaposed questions in which no conjunction morpheme stands, and marks it as an addition; no morpheme licenses it (rule 14's closing sentence).
Substantival adjective completed by the supplied generic *man*; headed on *poor*, which carries the lexeme (rule 31).
Articleless participle recast as a relative clause keeps the supplied relative with the attributive itself (rule 41), headed on the lexical verb.

The לְ before the infinitive already holds the written *to*, and no other morpheme answers to *how*, so it is a surplus function word (rules 52, 42). The margin's alternative rendering was read and set aside under rule 38.
לְ before the infinitive takes the written *to* (rule 52).

review_notes: Every source and target ID is partitioned exactly once.
